newsitem.title: CANADA: IPL says 2 Canada oil lines flowing 75 pct.
newsitem.headline: IPL says 2 Canada oil lines flowing 75 pct.

text.p: IPL Energy Inc unit Interprovincial Pipe Line said the two oil pipelines in Canada that were restarted on Tuesday were flowing at less than 75 percent of their total capacity.
IPL spokesman Alan Roth said Line 3, which runs to Superior, Wisconsin from Edmonton, Alberta was moving 18,869 barrels per hour, compared to its normal capacity of 26,417 barrels per hour.
Line 2B, which extends to Superior from Cromer, Manitoba, was flowing at 10,693 barrels per hour, down from its capacity of 18,869 barrels per hour.
The two pipelines were restarted earlier on Tuesday when partial power was restored to the company's Plummer pumping station in Minnesota.
Roth said the oil was flowing into IPL's tanks at Superior in hopes of restarting pipelines to eastern Canada and the U.S. Midwest later this afternoon.
He said that although operations to restart the huge pipeline system were going quicker than planned, predictions for when it would be back to capacity were not being moved up.
The company has said it could be at least Wednesday before the system was fully back on stream.
Roth said also that line 2A, which runs between Edmonton and Cromer, could be restarted later on Tuesday.
